spec_says: Second capability octet: bit7 SU beamformer, bit6 MU beamformer, bit5 UL MU-MIMO, bit4 UL MU-MIMO+OFDMA, bit3 DL MU-MIMO+OFDMA, bit2 UL OFDMA, bit1 DL OFDMA, bit0 reserved
upstream_does: Hand-packed one bit too low: dl_ofdma bit0, ul_ofdma bit1, dl_mimo_ofdma bit2, ul_mimo_ofdma bit3, ul_mimo bit4, mu_beamformer bit5, su_beamformer bit6; bit7 never set; spec reserved bit0 carries DL OFDMA
evidence: em.cpp:1443-1451 (b2 |= dl_ofdma_cap&1; ul_ofdma_cap<<1; dl_mimo_ofdma_cap<<2; ul_mimo_ofdma_cap<<3; ul_mimo_cap<<4; mu_beamformer_cap<<5; su_beamformer_cap<<6). Spec Table 32 rows 11-18 (SU bf=bit 7 ... DL OFDMA=bit 1, Reserved=bit 0). The struct em_base.h:1920-1926 (reserved:1 then dl_ofdma:1 ... su_beamformer:1) would place the fields at the spec positions if memcpy'd, so only the hand-packing is wrong. First octet (em.cpp:1437-1440: 160MHz bit0, 80+80 bit1, rx streams bits4-2, tx streams bits7-5) matches the spec.
notes: Coordinator-confirmed. Every capability flag in the second octet is misreported to a spec-compliant peer. The same function serves the normal and early AP Capability Report.
port_rule_reason: spec: second octet bit7 SU beamformer through bit1 DL OFDMA, bit0 reserved; each flag must sit at its spec bit.

spec_says: Supported HE MCS: Tx/Rx HE MCS Support field reordered into big-endian order (k = 4-12 octets)
upstream_does: Each 16-bit Tx and Rx MCS map is memcpy'd from host unsigned short, so it goes out little-endian on x86_64; order is Tx then Rx per set
evidence: em.cpp:1427-1434 (memcpy of tx_he_mcs then rx_he_mcs, sizeof(unsigned short)); em_base.h:1906-1909 (em_ap_he_mcs_maps_t). Spec Table 32 row 6.
notes: UNSURE: the spec text 'reordered ... into big-endian order' is ambiguous about the order of the Tx and Rx maps inside each 4-octet set (802.11 puts Rx before Tx). The 16-bit values being written in host (little-endian) order is certain. Nothing in src/ fills tx_he_mcs/rx_he_mcs from the HAL (only the CLI/DM paths read them), so the content may always be zero in practice.
port_rule_reason: spec 17.2.10: MCS maps are big-endian (SPEC). Open: Tx/Rx order, defined only in IEEE 802.11 [17]: Tx-then-Rx (upstream) or Rx-then-Tx.

spec_says: RUID(6), MCS_len k(1), k octets of MCS (k = 4-12), then the two capability octets directly after the k MCS octets
upstream_does: Receivers cast the value to the fixed em_ap_he_cap_t (MAX_MCS=3 sets, always 12 MCS octets) and memcpy sizeof(em_ap_he_cap_t)=21 octets; capability octets are read at fixed value offsets 19 and 20 whatever sprt_mcs_len says
evidence: em_capability.cpp:1584-1595 and :1863-1873 (reinterpret_cast<em_ap_he_cap_t*>, memcpy 21 bytes); em_base.h:1911-1927 (sprt_tx_rx_mcs[MAX_MCS]), MAX_MCS=3 em_base.h:94. Sender writes only sprt_mcs_len octets (em.cpp:1421-1434), so the capability octets sit at offsets 7+k and 8+k. Spec Table 32 rows 4-18.
notes: Any TLV with k < 12 (4 is the common ≤80 MHz case, including this port's own sender) has its capability bits taken from the bytes after the TLV (the following TLV or EOM) and the receiver copies 21 octets even when tlvLength is 13. The MCS field itself is not decoded as variable length either. Also affects em_msg.cpp:300-303 only for ruid (fine).
port_rule_reason: spec: RUID(6), MCS length k(1), k MCS octets (k 4-12), then the two capability octets directly after.

spec_says: tlvLength covers RUID + length octet + k MCS octets + 2 capability octets (k = 4-12)
upstream_does: Neither receiver checks tlvLength or sprt_mcs_len before reading the fixed struct; the early-report loop also does not check that a TLV length fits the remaining buffer, and tmp_len is an unsigned subtraction
evidence: em_capability.cpp:1522-1523 and :1719-1720 (early loop: tmp_len -= sizeof(em_tlv_t)+htons(tlv->len), no tlv->len <= tmp_len test); :1584-1595, :1863-1873 (no length test); em_msg.cpp:826,844 min length 10 is only enforced for mandatory TLVs (em_msg.cpp:683) and HE is optional. The full handler does check TLV bounds at :1788-1792.
notes: The early handler (handle_early_ap_cap_report) can walk off the packet on a truncated or oversized tlvLength; applies to every TLV in that handler, including the CAC TLV.
port_rule_reason: spec: tlvLength is the number of ensuing octets; RUID, length octet, k MCS octets and 2 capability octets.

spec_says: Supported HE MCS length k is 4-12 octets and equals the number of MCS octets that follow
upstream_does: mcs_count = sprt_mcs_len/4 clamped to 3 sets, but he_cap->sprt_mcs_len (the length octet already written at em.cpp:1418) is not clamped or rounded; a length not in {4,8,12} (including 0) gives a length octet that does not match the octets written
notes: Only reachable if the data model holds a nonstandard sprt_mcs_len.
port_rule_reason: spec: Supported HE MCS length k is variable, 4-12 octets.

spec_says: CC(2), Num_Radio(1), then per radio RUID(6), Num_Types(1), per type Method(1), Duration(3), Num_OpClass(1), per op class OpClass(1), Num_Chan(1), Num_Chan channel octets; all counts variable, no padding
upstream_does: Early-report receiver casts the value to the fixed em_cac_cap_t and indexes cac->radios[idx] at fixed stride sizeof(em_cac_cap_radio_t) (7 + 4 x method, method = 5 + 48 op classes x 18 octets, about 3.4 KB per radio by definition, em_base.h:2086-2103, 546-550), then memcpy's sizeof(cap_info->cac_cap) from that offset
evidence: em_capability.cpp:1611-1633 (reinterpret_cast<em_cac_cap_t*>, memcpy(&cap_info->cac_cap,&cac->radios[idx],sizeof(cap_info->cac_cap))). The sender (em.cpp:1959-1995) writes a packed variable-length layout. Spec Table (17.2.46) rows 4-13.
notes: Only RUID and Num_Types of the first radio line up. Method data, op class and channel lists for any radio are decoded at the wrong offsets, radios idx>=1 are read from the wrong place, and the memcpy reads several KB past the end of the TLV and likely past the received frame. The full handler (handle_ap_cap_report, :1893-1986) is correct, so only the Early AP Capability Report path (em_msg_type_early_ap_cap_rprt 0x8043) is affected. UNSURE: exact sizeof (comment at em_base.h:544-545 claims 150 and 607, but op_classes uses EM_MAX_OP_CLASS=48, not EM_MAX_CAC_OP_CLASS_PER_METHOD=8).
port_rule_reason: spec 17.2.46 gives packed CAC layout: CC, Num_Radio, per-radio RUID, Num_Types, Method, Duration, counts, channels; no padding. Port follows it.

spec_says: Duration: 3 octets, number of seconds; byte order not stated in the table (sender and full receiver use big-endian)
upstream_does: Early-report receiver reads the 3 octets through the packed bit-field cac_duration:24, i.e. little-endian, while the sender writes them big-endian (em.cpp:1972-1976) and the full receiver reads them big-endian (em_capability.cpp:1946-1947)
evidence: em_base.h:2088 (unsigned int cac_duration : 24); em_capability.cpp:1611-1633; em.cpp:1972-1976; em_capability.cpp:1945-1947. Spec row 9.
notes: Secondary to the FIELD_LAYOUT row above (offsets are already wrong there for radios beyond the first method).
port_rule_reason: spec 17.2.46 Duration: 3 octets, no byte order stated; keep upstream big-endian (sender and full receiver agree).

spec_says: Counts are bounded by tlvLength; Num_Radio, Num_Types, Num_OpClass, Num_Chan are 1-octet counts
upstream_does: Only radios_num <= 4 is checked; no check of tlvLength against the fixed struct size, method/op-class counts or channel counts before memcpy; same unchecked early-loop TLV walk as the HE row
notes: Over-read of untrusted input in the early handler.
port_rule_reason: spec: counts repeat fields within tlvLength; 1-octet counts, sized by tlvLength.

spec_says: Num_Types, Num_OpClass, Num_Chan are 1-octet counts matching what follows
upstream_does: Sender loops over cac_methods_num, op_classes_num and op->num straight from the data model with no clamp to the array sizes (4 methods, 48 op classes, 16 channels per class), so an out-of-range count reads past the arrays and emits more data than the buffer sizes imply
notes: Data originates in the local data model; the full receiver rejects such counts (em_capability.cpp:1933, :1951, :1966).
port_rule_reason: spec 17.2.46 Num_Types, Num_OpClass, Num_Chan are 1-octet counts; no smaller maximum, so accept 0-255 (upstream clamps to array sizes).

spec_says: As in the spec table: CC(2) Num_Radio(1) {RUID(6) Num_Types(1) {Method(1) Duration(3 big-endian) Num_OpClass(1) {OpClass(1) Num_Chan(1) Channel(Num_Chan)}}}
upstream_does: Sender (em.cpp:1909-2006) and the full receiver (em_capability.cpp:1893-1986) both use exactly this layout with 3-octet big-endian Duration and bounds checks against remaining length; Num_Radio==0 handled
notes: Scope: sender and full AP Capability Report receiver only. Sender only lists 5 GHz radios with cac_methods_num>0 (em.cpp:1938, :1954), a policy choice not a layout difference.
port_rule_reason: no difference

spec_says: Steering_Opportunity_Window: 2 octets, seconds; spec table does not state byte order (all other multi-octet fields in the port are network order)
upstream_does: Written in host (little-endian) order with a plain assignment while btm_dissoc_timer in the same struct uses htons
evidence: em_steering.cpp:485 (req->steering_opportunity_window = static_cast<unsigned short>(params->steer_opportunity_win)) versus :487 (htons for btm_dissoc_timer). Spec Table 51 row Steering_Opportunity_Window.
notes: Coordinator-confirmed. Only meaningful in Steering Opportunity mode (Request_Mode=0); mandate mode sends 0 (em_steering.cpp:480-483), which is the spec-ignored case. The receiver (em_steering.cpp:543-567) never reads the field, so the controller/agent pair of this port never exposes it.
port_rule_reason: spec 17.2.29 Steering_Opportunity_Window: 2 octets in seconds, no byte order stated; keep upstream little-endian (plain assignment).

spec_says: Target_BSSID_List_Count is 0 when Request_Mode=0 (Steering Opportunity) and the Target_BSSID/OpClass/Channel group is then omitted; STA_List_Count 0 means all STAs
upstream_does: Sender always writes sta_list_count=1 and target_bssid_list_count=1 with one target BSSID, op class and channel, even for Request_Mode=0
evidence: em_steering.cpp:488-493 (sta_list_count = 1, target_bssid_list_count = 1, target fields always filled), :476 (req_mode from params). Spec Table 51 Target_BSSID_List_Count row (rows 14-17).
notes: A compliant agent that follows the spec may reject or mishandle an opportunity request carrying a target list. For Request_Mode=1 the output is spec-conformant (one STA, one target).
port_rule_reason: spec: Target_BSSID_List_Count set to zero when Request_Mode=0 and the Target group is omitted.

spec_says: Variable layout: STA_List_Count (0..n) STA MACs, then Target_BSSID_List_Count (0, 1 or n) groups of Target_BSSID(6)+OpClass(1)+Channel(1)
upstream_does: Receiver casts the value to fixed em_steering_req_t (one STA MAC, one target group, 27 octets) and passes sizeof(em_steering_req_t) bytes to the bus event; sta_list_count and target_bssid_list_count are never read
evidence: em_steering.cpp:556 (reinterpret_cast<em_steering_req_t*>(&tlv->value)), :562 (io_process with sizeof(em_steering_req_t)); em_base.h:1168-1183 (single sta_mac_addr / target_bssids); consumer dm_easy_mesh_agent.cpp:836-862 uses only the one STA and one target. Spec Table 51 rows 12-17.
notes: With STA_List_Count=0 or >1, or Target_BSSID_List_Count=0 (opportunity mode), the later fields are read from the wrong octets or from beyond the TLV (a 19-octet TLV for one STA and no target is read as 27 octets). Request_Mode is also ignored by the agent, so an opportunity request is turned into a BTM request (dm_easy_mesh_agent.cpp:834-843 never tests req_mode).
port_rule_reason: spec: STA_MAC present STA_List_Count times; Target_BSSID, class and channel present Target_BSSID_List_Count times.

spec_says: BTM_Disassociation_Timer: 2 octets in TUs (written big-endian by this port's sender, htons)
upstream_does: Agent copies the network-order value directly into the 802.11 BSS Transition Management Request disassoc_timer, which is a little-endian le16, with no ntohs/conversion
evidence: dm_easy_mesh_agent.cpp:844 (memcpy of steer_req->btm_dissoc_timer into bss_tm_req.disassoc_timer); inc/ieee80211.h:1690 (le16 disassoc_timer); sender em_steering.cpp:487 (htons). Spec Table 51 row BTM_Disassociation_Timer.
notes: On x86_64 the timer put in the 802.11 frame is byte-swapped. Same function also assigns the timer to the 1-bit bss_termination_inc flag (line 839, 'todo' in source), which is a separate bug outside the TLV layout.
port_rule_reason: spec 17.2.29 BTM_Disassociation_Timer: 2 octets in TUs, no byte order stated; keep upstream big-endian TLV bytes; frame-side conversion not decided here.

spec_says: tlvLength = 13 + 6 x STA_List_Count + 8 x Target_BSSID_List_Count (BSSID 6, mode octet 1, window 2, timer 2, STA count 1, target count 1, then the lists)
upstream_does: No check of tlvLength or counts in handle_client_steering_req; the optional-TLV min length 15 in the message table is not enforced for optional TLVs
evidence: em_steering.cpp:543-567; em_msg.cpp:906 (optional, length 15; enforcement only for mandatory TLVs at em_msg.cpp:683).
notes: Over-read of fixed 27 octets from a shorter peer TLV.
port_rule_reason: spec: tlvLength is the number of ensuing octets, fixed by the STA and target list counts.

spec_says: Request_Mode bit7, Disassociation Imminent bit6, Abridged bit5, Link Removal Imminent bit4, bits3-0 reserved = 0
upstream_does: Bit positions match the spec (GCC: reserved:4 low, link_removal bit4, abridged bit5, dissoc_imminent bit6, req_mode bit7), but the reserved nibble is never assigned and the frame buffer is uninitialised stack
evidence: em_base.h:1170-1174; em_steering.cpp:168 (unsigned char buff[MAX_EM_BUFF_SZ], only the CMDU is memset at :195), :472-493 (req->reserved not written). Spec Table 51 rows 5-9.
notes: The other bit positions are correct. UNSURE: not checked whether the em_cmd/bus path zeroes the buffer before this function.
port_rule_reason: spec 17.2.29 BIT_LAYOUT: bit 7 Request_Mode, bit 6, bit 5, bit 4 as stated, bits 3-0 reserved = 0; port sends 0 there.

spec_says: Per mapping, after Expected_Duration(3): TID-to-Link_Mapping, 2 octets for every set bit of Link_Mapping_Presence_Indicator, then Reserved(7)
upstream_does: The TID-to-Link_Mapping octets are never written (TODO) and the record is a fixed sizeof(em_tid_to_link_mapping_t)=19 octets, so a peer expecting 2 x popcount(presence indicator) octets reads Reserved(7) and the next record at the wrong offsets
evidence: em_configuration.cpp:1687 ('//TODO: tid_to_link_map'), :1689-1690 (advance sizeof(em_tid_to_link_mapping_t)); em_base.h:3092-3106 (tid_to_link_map[0] zero length, reserved6[7]). Spec 17.2.102 TID-to-Link_Mapping row.
notes: Coordinator-confirmed. link_map_presence_ind is copied from the data model (em_configuration.cpp:1685), so any non-zero presence indicator produces an inconsistent TLV; with presence indicator 0 the layout is correct.
port_rule_reason: spec: TID-to-Link_Mapping 2 octets per set bit of Link_Mapping_Presence_Indicator, then 7 reserved octets.

spec_says: Num_Mapping: 2 octets (spec table does not state byte order; every TLV length and count elsewhere in the port is network order)
upstream_does: Num_Mapping written in host (little-endian) order with a plain assignment, no htons
evidence: em_configuration.cpp:1674 (tid_to_link_map_policy->num_mapping = tid_to_link_info.num_mapping); em_base.h:3115. Spec row Num_Mapping.
notes: UNSURE of the spec's intended byte order since the table is silent, but a count of 1 goes out as 01 00, which a big-endian reader sees as 256. The loop on line 1677 also uses the same host-order field.
port_rule_reason: spec 17.2.102 Num_Mapping: 2 octets, no byte order stated (only the presence indicator is named big-endian); keep upstream little-endian.

spec_says: TID-to-Link Control bit 3 (spec: Expected_Duration_Present = bit 3 of the control octet) tells the receiver whether Expected_Duration is meaningful
upstream_does: Sender sets direction, default_link_mapping, map_switch_time_present and link_map_size but never copies expected_dur_present to exp_dur_present, so that bit is whatever the uninitialised buffer held
evidence: em_configuration.cpp:1679-1686 (no assignment of exp_dur_present); em_base.h:3098 (exp_dur_present:1), em_base.h:2911 (expected_dur_present in the data model). Spec rows Expected_Duration_Present / Expected_Duration.
notes: Bit position itself matches the spec (direction bits 7-6, default bit 5, switch time bit 4, expected duration bit 3, link map size bit 2, reserved bits 1-0).
port_rule_reason: spec: Expected_Duration_Present is bit 3 of the TID-to-Link control octet; port must set it.

spec_says: Reserved bits and fields must be zero: reserved bits 6-0 of the is_bSTA_Config octet, of the Negotiation octet and of the addRemove octet, bits 1-0 of the control octet, Reserved(22) and Reserved(7)
upstream_does: Only the named bits are written. The destination is the stack buffer in send_topology_response_msg, which is not zeroed (only the CMDU header is memset), so all reserved bits and reserved3[22]/reserved6[7] carry stack garbage
evidence: em_configuration.cpp:1701 (unsigned char buff[MAX_EM_BUFF_SZ + MAX_EM_BUFF_SZ], no full memset; memset only at :1733 for the CMDU), :1670-1686 (assigns named fields only); em_base.h:3092-3117 (reserved1..reserved6).
notes: Layout and positions are right (is_bsta_config bit 7, negotiation bit 7, add_remove bit 7). Impact is nonzero reserved values on the wire.
port_rule_reason: spec: reserved bits of is_bSTA_Config, Negotiation and addRemove shown as 0; reserved octets value unstated.

spec_says: Num_Mapping is the number of records; if is_bSTA_Config = 1, Num_Mapping is 0
upstream_does: num_mapping is copied from the data model without checking it against EM_MAX_AP_MLD (64) or against the output buffer, and is not forced to 0 when is_bsta_config is 1
notes: Data-model driven; an out-of-range count reads past the array.
port_rule_reason: spec: Num_Mapping set to zero when is_bSTA_Config = 1; EM_MAX_AP_MLD bound is not spec text.

spec_says: Direction: 2 bits (bits 0-1 of the TID-to-Link Control field of the IEEE 802.11 element; values are defined by 802.11, the table lists none)
upstream_does: Data model holds direction as bool, so only 0 and 1 can be sent; value 2 (bidirectional in 802.11be) cannot be expressed
notes: UNSURE: depends on 802.11be Direction encoding, which is outside the extraction.
port_rule_reason: spec 17.2.102 Direction values come only from IEEE 802.11be (unavailable). Reading A: all 2-bit values; reading B: only 0 and 1, as upstream bool.

spec_says: TLV may be received by an agent in Topology Response / policy flows
upstream_does: No code parses em_tlv_type_tid_to_link_map_policy; only the builder and the message-table entry (labelled 17.2.97 in the comment) reference it
evidence: git grep of em_tlv_type_tid_to_link_map_policy and em_tid_to_link_map_policy_t at the pin: src/em/config/em_configuration.cpp:1664-1666 and src/em/em_msg.cpp:784 (optional, min length 64, not enforced).
notes: Receiver side only; the sender rows above are implemented.
port_rule_reason: spec: NOT_IMPLEMENTED row, no upstream bytes to keep; agent-side TLV receipt follows spec text.

spec_says: Num_Service (1 octet) then Num_Service x Supported_Service (1 octet each); tlvLength=1+Num_Service
upstream_does: Writes value[0]=count (1, or 2 for EM+), then one octet per service; len=htons(2) or htons(3); receiver requires tlv_len==1+num, copies num octets
notes: Core layout matches. Single-octet fields so no byte order issue. Senders memcpy 1 byte of a 4-byte enum (em_configuration.cpp:1772,4429): fine on little-endian only.
port_rule_reason: no difference

spec_says: Supported_Service values 0x00 Controller, 0x01 Agent, 0x02-0xFF reserved
upstream_does: When the peer/this device is EM+ the TLV carries two entries: {ctrl/agent, 0xA0 emplus_ctrl or 0xA1 emplus_agent}, i.e. values in the reserved range
notes: Vendor extension using reserved values. Spec-compliant peer should ignore reserved entries; a strict peer could reject the TLV. Only emitted when is_emplus_agent / peer_is_emplus.
port_rule_reason: spec: Supported_Service 0x00 Controller, 0x01 Agent, 0x02-0xFF reserved; port follows the defined values.

spec_says: Num_Service is 1 octet (0-255 entries); each entry independent
upstream_does: get_supported_service returns false (TLV treated as absent) when Num_Service > EM_MAX_SERVICE (8)
notes: Only 2 service values are defined so unlikely to matter. Also requires tlv_len == 1+Num_Service exactly (em_msg.cpp:112), which is consistent with the spec table. copy_len code (em_msg.cpp:107-110,118-120) is redundant.
port_rule_reason: spec: Num_Service 1 octet; counts above 8 are valid, so the EM_MAX_SERVICE cap is over-strict.

spec_says: Num_Service gives entry count; entries must lie within tlvLength
upstream_does: handle_bss_config_req_msg does memcpy(&service_type,&tlv->value[1],sizeof(em_service_type_t)) = 4 bytes (enum) without checking tlv->len or Num_Service
notes: Over-reads up to 3 octets past a 2-octet value; result is never used afterwards (service_type is a dead local in that function); only first entry considered. Message-level validate() requires min TLV size 5 for mandatory supported_service (em_msg.cpp:1077,683).
port_rule_reason: spec: Supported_Service is 1 octet, present Num_Service times, so entries must lie within tlvLength.

spec_says: Num_Service (1 octet) then Num_Service x Searched_Service (1 octet); 0x00 = Controller
upstream_does: Writes {1, em_service_type_ctrl(0x00)} via add_tlv, length 2
notes: No receiver at the pin: no code parses em_tlv_type_searched_service other than the presence list in em_msg.cpp:718 (optional, min 5, which is not enforced for optional TLVs). So the controller does not filter autoconf responses on Searched Service. Only sender is autoconf search.
port_rule_reason: no difference

spec_says: Single field: RUID, 6 octets; tlvLength=6
upstream_does: Copies 6-octet radio MAC with memcpy; len=htons(6); receiver memcpy 6 octets from value
notes: Only sender is the WSC M2 builder. No byte order concern for a MAC.
port_rule_reason: no difference

spec_says: tlvLength is exactly 6
upstream_does: get_radio_id memcpy's 6 octets from value without checking tlv length >= 6; message validate() only enforces a minimum TLV size of 4 (3-octet header + 1) for radio_id in WSC M2
notes: Short TLV (len 1..5) passes validate and over-reads up to 5 octets beyond the TLV (still bounded by caller buffer in most cases). Min should be 9 as already used at em_msg.cpp:954. UNSURE whether the over-read can exceed the received buffer.
port_rule_reason: spec 17.2.3 tlvLength is exactly 6; port requires length 6 and does not read beyond it.

spec_says: Num_Radio(1) then per radio: RUID(6), Num_BSS(1), then per BSS: AP_MAC(6), SSID Length(1), SSID(n)
upstream_does: Packed structs em_ap_op_bss_t / em_ap_op_bss_radio_t / em_ap_operational_bss_t give exactly that order; sender fills via pointers, receiver walks the same way
notes: Field order, sizes, repeat structure and zero-BSS case (no BSS group written) match. All fields are single octets or MACs, so no byte order issue. tlvLength written htons(tlv_len).
port_rule_reason: no difference

spec_says: SSID Length = n, SSID is n octets (the SSID itself, max 32 octets, no terminator)
upstream_does: SSID Length = strlen(ssid)+1 and SSID field includes the trailing NUL; 32-char SSID is sent with length 33
evidence: em_configuration.cpp:1100-1103 (bss->ssid_len = strlen+1); also dead variant :1049-1051; Table 17.2.4 rows 5-6
notes: Every BSS entry sent in Topology Response carries an extra NUL octet in SSID. A spec-compliant receiver sees SSID with embedded trailing 0x00 (and 33 octets for a 32-char SSID), so SSID comparison/display against configured SSID can fail. The upstream receiver tolerates it (em_configuration.cpp:2269-2275 clamps/terminates) so the problem only appears with a compliant peer. Also strncpy(bss->ssid, ssid, sizeof(ssid_t)) at :1100 zero-pads up to sizeof(ssid_t) (33 per EM_MAX_SSID_LEN, UNSURE: ssid_t typedef not located) octets past the SSID, possibly beyond the end of the TLV.
port_rule_reason: spec 17.2.4 SSID Length = n with n SSID octets, no terminator; port sends n, not strlen+1.

spec_says: Num_Radio, Num_BSS, SSID Length must be consistent with tlvLength
upstream_does: handle_ap_operational_bss ignores len (and is passed tlv->len in network order, em_configuration.cpp:2473); radios_num, bss_num and ssid_len are used unchecked to advance pointers; new BSS written to dm->m_bss[dm->m_num_bss] with no array bound check
evidence: em_configuration.cpp:2229-2303 (2249,2252,2255-2256,2289-2293), 2473; em_msg.cpp:304-306 reads ap->radios[0].ruid without any length check
notes: Untrusted counts from a peer can drive reads past the received frame and unbounded writes into m_bss[]. Frame-level TLV bounds are checked by validate() (em_msg.cpp:656-664) but inner structure is not.
port_rule_reason: spec: Num_Radio and Num_BSS repeat fields and SSID Length n set the SSID size; all bounded by tlvLength.

spec_says: Num_BSS may be 0 (BSS group omitted); minimum TLV is Num_Radio (+ per radio RUID, Num_BSS)

upstream_does: packed em_client_assoc_ctrl_req_t memcpy'd: bssid[6], assoc_control, validity_period (htons, em_steering.cpp:79; ntohs at em_agent.cpp:811), sta_count, sta_list; tlv len = 10+6*N (:132-136,:138). Field order, sizes, repeat and byte order match

spec_says: Table 57: fixed body STA_MAC(6)+7 x 4-octet counters = 34 octets; a shorter TLV is malformed
upstream_does: Receiver casts tlv->value to em_assoc_sta_traffic_stats_t (34 octets, packed) and reads all fields; the handler is passed only tlv->value (no length) so tlv->len is never compared with 34. Only the enclosing check tlv_total <= remaining (em_metrics.cpp:1056-1060) applies. In AP Metrics Response the TLV is 'optional' (em_msg.cpp:962) so em_msg_t::validate() does not enforce a minimum length either (only mandatory members are length-checked, em_msg.cpp:683); only Client Disassociation Stats (em_msg.cpp:1112, min 37) enforces it, and that message has no parser for this TLV.
notes: A short TLV makes the receiver read up to 34 octets past the TLV start, i.e. into following TLVs / beyond the frame end if it is the last TLV before EOM-less data. Layout, field order and network byte order otherwise match the spec (sender uses htonl for all 7 counters, receiver ntohl; struct em_base.h:1344-1353 and 1773-1784 are packed MAC+7x u32).
port_rule_reason: spec: body is STA_MAC 6 octets plus seven 4-octet counters, 34 octets; shorter TLV is malformed.

spec_says: Reason_Code 0x00 is Reserved; defined values are 0x01-0x06. The Error Code TLV reports a failure condition (STA associated / not associated / capability failure / backhaul steering rejects).
upstream_does: Several senders emit the TLV unconditionally with reason 0x00 (reserved): Client Capability Report always appends it with reason 0 (em_capability.cpp:608,677); the 1905 Ack built in em_configuration.cpp:1953-1996 always carries reason 0 with a zero STA MAC (called with sta_mac=0 at em_configuration.cpp:2885); create_error_code_tlv in metrics sets reason 0x00 unless is_associated (em_metrics.cpp:2396-2400, sta_found is ignored so 0x02 is never sent) and is committed unconditionally in Associated STA Link Metrics Response (:1253) and Beacon Metrics Response (:1435).
notes: A spec-compliant receiver may treat a reserved reason code (or an Error Code TLV in a success response, e.g. Client Capability Report) as a failure. UNSURE which of these enclosing messages the spec allows an Error Code TLV in on success; the reserved value 0x00 itself is not allowed.
port_rule_reason: spec: Reason_Code 0x00 is Reserved (defined values 0x01-0x06); a reserved value must not be sent, so port does not emit 0x00.

spec_says: Reason codes 0x03 (client capability report unspecified failure) and 0x04-0x06 (backhaul steering request rejected: channel / signal / auth-assoc)
upstream_does: No sender or receiver for 0x03-0x06: em_steering.cpp contains no Backhaul Steering Response builder/parser using the Error Code TLV, and the Client Capability Report sender only uses reason 0. Receiver only recognises 0x01 and 0x02 (em_metrics.cpp:263-267) and only in the Associated STA Link Metrics Response path; em_msg.cpp lists the TLV as optional in bh_steering_rsp (:940) but nothing consumes it.
evidence: src/em/em_msg.cpp:940,948,976,1174; src/em/metrics/em_metrics.cpp:261-269; git grep em_tlv_type_error_code shows only the sites cited above
notes: Feature gap rather than wire-format difference.

spec_says: tlvLength = 7; STA_MAC valid only for reason 0x01/0x02; TLVs must lie within the frame
upstream_does: Receiver reads tlv->value[0] and tlv->value[1..6] without checking tlv->len >= 7. The TLV walk loops use 'tmp_len -= sizeof(em_tlv_t)+ntohs(tlv->len)' on a size_t with only a 'tmp_len > 0' loop guard, so a TLV length larger than the remaining bytes wraps tmp_len and the walk continues past the frame. The em_msg_t::validate() failure at the top of the function is ignored (return -1 commented out). Only the first Error Code TLV is used (break at :268).
upstream_receiver: src/em/metrics/em_metrics.cpp:261-269 (inside handle_associated_sta_link_metrics_resp, 227-300); presence-only scan at src/em/metrics/em_metrics.cpp:2461
notes: Untrusted-input hardening issue; for well-formed 7-octet TLVs behaviour matches spec.
port_rule_reason: spec: tlvLength 7; STA_MAC meaningful only for reason 0x01 or 0x02, otherwise ignored by recipient.

spec_says: Reason_Code is a single octet
upstream_does: Both builders do memcpy(tmp, &val, sizeof(unsigned char)) where val is an int: copies the low-address byte of the int, which is the low byte only on little-endian hosts.
notes: Correct on x86_64 (target); would write 0 on a big-endian host for values < 256. Cosmetic for the port.
port_rule_reason: spec: Reason_Code is a single octet; port writes exactly one octet regardless of host byte order.

spec_says: Table 59: one octet; bit 7 = Report Independent Channel Scans, bits 6-0 reserved; TLV (zero or one) present with length 1
upstream_does: Struct em_channel_scan_rprt_policy_t declares reserved:7 then rprt_ind_ch_scan:1, which GCC packs to bit 7 / bits 6-0, so the octet matches the spec (sender sets reserved=0). However, if no channel-scan policy object is found in the data model the builder emits no value octets: create_chan_scan_report_policy_tlv returns 0 and the caller still commits the TLV header with tlv->len = 0 (the TLV is always added when !is_set_policy).
notes: Only when the DM has no em_policy_id_type_channel_scan entry. Receiver here requires len == 1 (:822) so a zero-length TLV is ignored by this implementation, but a spec-compliant peer would see a malformed 0xA4 TLV. Bit layout and reserved handling are OK (BIT_LAYOUT: no difference).
port_rule_reason: spec: one policy octet, bit 7 Report Independent Channel Scans, bits 6-0 reserved; port emits that octet.

spec_says: Table 59: tlvLength listed as 'Variable' (2 octets length field); single policy octet defined
upstream_does: Receiver silently ignores the TLV unless tlv->len == sizeof(em_channel_scan_rprt_policy_t) == 1; a TLV with trailing octets (e.g. future extension) is dropped rather than parsed from the first octet. Reserved bits 6-0 are ignored, as required.
notes: UNSURE whether spec intends more than 1 octet; the table only defines one octet.
port_rule_reason: UNSURE: spec gives tlvLength as Variable yet defines one policy octet; readings: exactly one octet, or extensible with trailing octets (receiver drops len != 1).

spec_says: Table 60: Num_Radio(1); per radio RUID(6), [On Boot Only bit7 | Scan Impact bits6-5 | reserved bits4-0](1), Minimum Scan Interval(4), Num_OpClass(1); per op class Operating Class(1), Num_Chan(1), Channel List(Num_Chan)
upstream_does: Wire layout matches: struct em_channel_scan_cap_radio_t is packed ruid[6], {reserved:5, scan_impact:2, boot_only:1}, u32 min_scan_interval, u8 op_classes_num (em_base.h:2064-2071); GCC places boot_only at bit 7, scan_impact at bits 6-5. Sender writes min_scan_interval with htonl, receiver ntohl; op class entries written byte by byte (class, num, channels). Receiver computes radio header as sizeof(struct)-sizeof(op_classes) = 12 octets and bounds-checks each op class / channel list against len.
notes: Informational row confirming bit layout, byte order and repeat structure; differences are listed in the following rows.
port_rule_reason: no difference

spec_says: Num_Radio = number of radios for which capabilities are declared (all radios of the Agent)
upstream_does: Sender clamps Num_Radio to EM_MAX_BANDS (3) although the agent can hold EM_MAX_RADIO_PER_AGENT (4) radios, so a 4th radio is silently not reported.
notes: Only affects agents with more than 3 radios.
port_rule_reason: spec: Num_Radio counts the radios for which channel scan capabilities are declared; no cap of 3 stated.

spec_says: TLV carries Num_Radio and complete per-radio blocks (minimum 1 octet)
upstream_does: If dm->get_radio_cap(ruid) or get_radio_cap_info() is NULL for any radio, create_channelscan_tlv returns 0 after Num_Radio and earlier radios were already written; the caller then sets tlv->len = 0, producing an empty 0xA5 TLV (Num_Radio octet missing).
notes: Error path only (capability data not yet populated).
port_rule_reason: spec: TLV begins with Num_Radio octet then per-radio blocks; the error path emitting an empty TLV breaks this.

spec_says: Minimum valid TLV: Num_Radio = 0 (1 octet) or one radio with Num_OpClass = 0 (13 octets)
upstream_does: Message validation marks the TLV mandatory (profile > 1) with minimum total length 17 (header 3 + 14 value octets), so spec-valid TLVs shorter than 14 octets (Num_Radio=0, or radios with Num_OpClass=0) are rejected by em_msg_t::validate().
notes: Edge case; realistic TLVs contain at least one op class (>= 15 value octets).
port_rule_reason: spec: Num_Radio is 1 octet; Num_Radio=0 is a valid value, so the minimum valid TLV is 1 octet.

spec_says: Num_OpClass up to 255 and Num_Chan up to 255 per op class (single octets)
upstream_does: Receiver stores at most EM_MAX_OPCLASS (64) op classes and truncates each channel list to EM_MAX_CHANNELS_IN_LIST (64) channels; excess is skipped correctly in the byte stream but dropped from the data model. Handler's return value (truncation errors) is ignored by the caller, so partially updated state is kept. For unknown RUIDs the radio block is skipped, not stored.
notes: Parsing of the byte stream stays in sync; only storage is capped.
port_rule_reason: spec: Num_OpClass and Num_Chan are single octets; parse all entries, storage cap is a local detail.

spec_says: Fresh = bit 7, bits 6-0 reserved; Num_Radio; per radio RUID, Num_OpClass, per opclass OpClass, Num_Chan, channel list
upstream_does: Struct em_channel_scan_req_t declares reserved:7 then perform_fresh_scan:1 so Fresh lands on bit 7 (GCC LSB-first); sender sets reserved=0, Fresh=1 only if num_op_classes>0; field order, sizes and 1-byte counts match spec; TLV type 0xA6 matches
notes: Layout of the single-radio, single-opclass-per-TLV form matches. Sender emits Num_Radio=1 and (break at line 226) at most one OpClass.
port_rule_reason: no difference

spec_says: Num_Radio may be >1: RUID..Channel List group repeats Num_Radio times
upstream_does: Receiver rejects the whole request unless num_radios == 1 (CHANNEL_SCAN_SUPPORTED_RADIO_COUNT); the group is not looped. It also ignores the RUID in the TLV body when filling params (uses get_radio_interface_mac()); the RUID is only peeked at em_msg.cpp:320-327 to pick the radio
evidence: em_channel.cpp:56,2212-2215,2217; em_msg.cpp:320-327; spec 17.2.39 row 3-4 and 'above 5 fields present Num_Radio times'
notes: A spec-compliant controller sending one TLV covering several radios gets no scan and no ACK (return -1 before send_1905_ack_message). Controller side of upstream always sends 1 radio so intra-upstream works.
port_rule_reason: spec: RUID through Channel List group is present Num_Radio times; port must loop, not reject.

spec_says: Bits 6-0 of first octet are Reserved (receiver should ignore reserved bits)
upstream_does: Receiver returns -1 (message dropped, no ACK) if any of bits 6-0 is non-zero (CHANNEL_SCAN_RESERVED_BITS_MASK = 0x7F)
notes: Stricter than spec; breaks if a newer peer sets a bit defined later.
port_rule_reason: EasyMesh §3.1.2: recipient ignores reserved bits; port ignores bits 6-0 instead of dropping the message.

spec_says: Num_Chan is 1 octet (0..255); 0 = all channels in the opclass
upstream_does: Receiver rejects the message if num_channels > EM_MAX_CHANNELS_IN_LIST (64) or num_op_classes > EM_MAX_OP_CLASS (48); Num_Chan=0 is accepted and honoured downstream (is_requested_scan_result: empty list = all channels)
notes: Limits are generous for real op classes (max 59 channels in 6 GHz); rejection of the whole message on excess rather than ignoring. Bounds checks against payload_end and exact parsed_len == tlv len are present and correct.
port_rule_reason: spec: Num_Chan and Num_OpClass are 1 octet with no smaller maximum; port accepts every width-allowed value, not upstream's 64/48 caps.

spec_says: If Fresh=0, Num_OpClass shall be 0 and remaining fields omitted; Fresh=1 requests a fresh scan
upstream_does: Sender sets Fresh=1 only when an op class matching the radio band was found, otherwise Fresh=0/Num_OpClass=0 (stored results); it cannot request a fresh scan with Num_OpClass=0. Receiver rejects Fresh=0 with Num_OpClass!=0 (correct). Receiver never uses the Fresh bit otherwise: Fresh=1 with Num_OpClass=0 is treated like Fresh=0 (no scan triggered, stored results returned)
notes: Semantic, not wire layout. UNSURE whether spec defines Fresh=1 with Num_OpClass=0.
port_rule_reason: UNSURE: spec requires Num_OpClass 0 when Fresh=0 but is silent on Fresh=1 with Num_OpClass 0 (no-op scan or invalid).

spec_says: Timestamp Length (1 octet) then Timestamp string of that many octets
upstream_does: value[0] = strlen(date_time), then the string bytes; TLV len = strlen+1 (matches); one extra NUL byte is memcpy'd past the TLV end (overwritten by next TLV header, harmless); type 0xA8 matches
notes: Layout and length encoding match the spec.
port_rule_reason: no difference

spec_says: String per date-and-time typedef; shall include time-secfrac and time-offset (pattern \d{4}-..T..:..:..\.\d+Z|[+-]\d{2}:\d{2})
